Location charges

What each location is charged under the cost rules. Stores, the regional loaner pools (761–768) and the HQ departments (730, 735, 510, 530, 590, 620, 705, 740) carry fuel, the fixed flat rate and $0.425 per truck mile (LD vehicles – pickups, cars and cargo vans – get no mileage charge). Distribution, Millwork, 355CD and 355 Reload carry actual cost: fuel, maintenance, depreciation, lease, registration, taxes, Geotab and Lytx. 450 Millwork and Distribution 353, 356, 359 and 489 are on straight P&L, so they show the same actual cost in both views.

Actual cost

What McCoy's actually spends. Fuel, maintenance, depreciation, lease, registration, taxes and telematics for every asset, wherever it sits. Flat rates and mileage charges are internal and left out, so only a real change in miles, fuel or fleet size moves this number.

Moves in this scenario

Pick a new location for any asset in the table below, or terminate or relocate it out. Costs update immediately using the destination's rules. Changes are kept in this browser only; use Export to Excel to save a copy and Import scenario to load one back.

How a move works

  • The destination's rules apply. At a store an asset is charged its flat rate (and $0.425 per mile for trucks other than pickups, cars and cargo vans). At an actual-cost location it carries its fuel, maintenance, depreciation, lease and fees.
  • Work stays with the location. Demand is what the history shows, so a moved truck brings no new work. The miles it drove stay at its origin and pass to the trucks that remain there, at the fuel rate of the truck that left. At the destination, the location's existing miles are shared across all its trucks.
  • Forklifts carry their propane. TMFLs, trailers and other equipment have no separate fuel.
  • Terminate or relocate out. The asset's costs leave the forecast from its effective month. Terminating saves the company its maintenance, depreciation, lease and fees; relocating out moves them outside McCoy's 2027 plan. Its work stays with the remaining units at the location.
  • No store rate. Golf carts, scissor lifts, cars, van trailers and other equipment have no store flat rate. A move of one of these to a store is flagged.
  • Effective month. Every change starts in the month you pick (default January).

2027 replacements and sale proceeds

  • Old unit. Depreciation, lease and registration & taxes run through the delivery month and stop the month after. Fuel and maintenance carry over to the new unit.
  • New unit. Owned, straight-line from the delivered cost: 60 months for trucks, 84 for forklifts and TMFLs, starting in the delivery month (month 1). Registration & taxes are recalculated from the new cost (taxes 0.0667% a month; registration 0.05% for trucks).
  • Sale. The old unit sells the month after delivery. Price is the median of 2025–2026 healthy sales (damaged units excluded) for the most specific match with at least 3 sales: same type, brand and age; then type and brand; then type and age; then type.
  • Proceeds lines. Sale proceeds are split by asset type following the Proceeds Type mapping: Vehicle Heavy, Vehicle Light, Forklift and 18 Wheeler.
  • Gain or loss = expected price − book value at the sale month. It is a one-time item and is not included in location charges or actual cost. Leased units go back to the lessor, so they have no sale.

By month

Delivery month drives capital and depreciation; sale month (one month later) drives proceeds and gain or loss.

Method

  • Scope. Every active asset on the asset roster except 950 Rio Truss. The roster sets location and in-service date. 033 Pharr, 355CD and 355 Pharr Reload sit in Region 05; regional loaner pools (761–768) sit in their regions. 765 (Region 05) and 768 (Region 08) have no assets on the roster, so each carries one fuel-only line at the average of the other pools' fuel (2,879 gal/yr).
  • New store 122 Canyon Lake (Region 07). Opens mid-June 2027; its 9 planned assets (2 24' TA Flatbeds, 2 TMFLs, 3 6K forklifts, 1 8K forklift, 1 pickup) are charged from July. Miles, fuel and propane use the Region 07 median for each type; depreciation, maintenance and registration, taxes, Geotab and Lytx use the median of same-type units bought 2024 or later.
  • Cost rules. Stores (Regions 01–08), regional loaner pools (761–768) and HQ departments (730, 735, 510, 530, 590, 620, 705, 740): fuel + flat rate, plus $0.425 per mile for trucks (not LD vehicles: pickups, cars and cargo vans). Actual cost (Distribution 353/356/359/489, Millwork 450, 355CD and 355 Reload): fuel + maintenance + depreciation + lease + registration, taxes, Geotab and Lytx.
  • Rentals. Truck and forklift rental invoices (work order categories "Truck - Rental" and "Forklift - Rental", Oct 2025–Sep 2026) are taken out of maintenance and shown as Truck rental and Forklift rental, spread evenly by month and kept with the unit they were charged to. Like maintenance, they count in location charges only at actual-cost locations. The recurring forklift rental at 011 South Austin was turned in, so it is not carried into 2027.
  • Adaptive export. The Adaptive export button (header and every tab) downloads the forecast as shown, scenario changes and replacements included, in the Adaptive import format: Account Code, Level Code, Split Label, 01/2027–12/2027. Stores 001–122, 387 Window Delivery, loaner pools 761–768 and 730/735/900 export their location charges (fuel, flat rate and mileage charge to 6645_AllocatedFleet for stores and pools); their sale proceeds post to 735 Fleet. Distribution 353/356/359, Millwork 450, 489 EWP, 355 Centralized Delivery and 355 Pharr - Reload export actual cost, and their sale proceeds post to their own level. All forklift maintenance goes to 6602_ForkliftRepair_Maintenance. Department fuel accounts 510 Information Services, 530 People Development, 620 Marketing and 740 Risk Management export in the charges format to their own levels. Sale proceeds export as a deduction (negative).
  • Lease lines. Lease payments are split by asset type following the Lease Type mapping: Truck (trucks, tractors and trailers), Forklift (forklifts, TMFLs and equipment) and LD (pickups, cars, cargo vans, millwork and open-air trailers).
  • Maintenance lines. Maintenance is split into four lines by asset type, following the Maintenance Type mapping: Truck (flatbeds, slide flatbeds, conveyors, van bodies, tractors), LD (pickups, cars, cargo vans, millwork and open-air trailers), Forklift (yard and truck-mounted forklifts, order pickers, reach trucks, scissor lifts, golf carts, light towers, sweepers, generators) and Trailer (flatbed, pup and van trailers, rolling tarps).
  • Depreciation lines. Depreciation is split into four lines by asset type, following the Depreciation Type mapping: Vehicle Heavy (24' TA Flatbeds, slide flatbeds, conveyors, van bodies), Vehicle Light (pickups, cars, cargo vans, millwork and open-air trailers), Forklifts (yard and truck-mounted forklifts, order pickers, reach trucks, scissor lifts, golf carts, light towers, sweepers, generators) and 18 Wheeler (tractors, flatbed, pup and van trailers, rolling tarps).
  • Truck fuel and LD fuel. LD fuel is the fuel for light-duty vehicles (pickups, cars and cargo vans); truck fuel is everything else. Both use actual gallons by location for Nov 2025–Oct 2026 (fuel card accounts plus the three onsite tanks: 359 Mc Reload incl. 489, 356 Midland, 353 Dayton), month by month. Stores and all other locations are priced at the 2027 blended rate ($5.198 Jan → $3.735 Dec); Distribution (353, 356, 359, 489) at the 2027 diesel forecast price (Jan $5.41 → Dec $3.73). Each location's trucks are scaled so the location matches its actual gallons, split by each truck's own fuel history; a moved truck takes its share with it. Fuel stays with the card account that bought it, so loaner-pool accounts (761–768) carry the fuel bought on them. Accounts with fuel but no trucks on the roster (765, 768 and accounts 510, 530, 620, 740) carry a fuel-only line. 068 is closed and left out. 900 has no account of its own, so its trucks carry no fuel. Planned store 122 uses Region 07 medians from July.
  • Forklift fuel. AmeriGas propane gallons by location for the same months, split evenly across each location's forklifts × the propane planning price. Distribution locations use the propane gallons in the 2027 Distribution fuel forecast. Shared accounts: 033 covers 033, 355 and 355CD; 359 covers 359 and 489 EWP. The 900 airport tractor runs on Jet A, which is not tracked; it is very low use and carries no fuel. TMFLs, trailers and other equipment have no separate fuel.
  • Miles. Geotab miles Oct 2025–Sep 2026; blank months are treated as missing, and the reported-month average × 12 is used. Loaner IDs are matched on the asset number.
  • Maintenance. Vendor invoices Oct 2025–Sep 2026 (all invoice statuses, credits netted), spread across 2027 by the company-wide monthly pattern. Registration work orders are excluded where the fee file supplies registration.
  • Depreciation. Monthly amount from the March 2026 file (components summed by asset); provided costs ÷ term for new units. The in-service month is month 1; trucks and trailers stop after 60 months; forklifts, TMFLs, golf carts, scissor lifts and other equipment after 84. Leased assets get no depreciation.
  • Leases. Fixed monthly rate from the lease file; 747104 ($250) and 747106 ($150) are on holding rentals; rates not yet supplied use the 2020 Toyota batch rate of $447.11. All leases run through Dec 2027.
  • Registration, taxes, Geotab and Lytx. Monthly per asset from the company-wide fee file (all 1,441 assets). 15 assets with no original value in that file are estimated with its own formulas (taxes 0.0667% and vehicle/trailer registration 0.05% of cost per month), using the cost of the same type at the closest purchase age (same year when available); they are listed below. Charged at actual-cost locations; at stores they are built into the flat rate. The actual-cost view carries them wherever the asset sits.
